k8s-lab-main.name: Kubernetes lab control plane (Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image, MicroK8s 1.32)
k8s-lab-main.notes: The control plane of the k8s-lab (vms/labs/k8s-lab/): MicroK8s 1.32 from the snap store, also a node that runs pods. At every boot on the lab segment /usr/local/sbin/k8s-lab-node pins the kubelet and the API server to 172.20.6.1 (every VM's NAT NIC is 10.0.2.15), points Calico at k8s-lan and publishes the fixed join token the workers use. NodePort 30080 is forwarded to http://127.0.0.1:8089 on the host. Ubuntu 24.04 minimal cloud image; the install downloads the snap (about 200 MB). Inspired by manzolo/multipass-microk8s-cluster-demo.

write_files.content:
[Unit]
Description=k8s-lab: this node's place in the cluster on k8s-lan
After=network-online.target snapd.service snap.microk8s.daemon-kubelite.service
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
TimeoutStartSec=0
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/k8s-lab-node

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

post_install_run: sudo systemctl enable k8s-lab-node.service    # after the script exists: the install boot has nothing to run
sudo microk8s kubectl get nodes | grep -q ' Ready '

k8s-lab-node1.name: Kubernetes lab worker (Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image, MicroK8s 1.32)
k8s-lab-node1.notes: A worker of the k8s-lab (vms/labs/k8s-lab/): MicroK8s 1.32 that joins k8s-lab-main (172.20.6.1) with --worker at its first boot on the lab segment and stays joined. Ubuntu 24.04 minimal cloud image.
